adjudications.reasoning: The rule is a penalty-free preference (rule_kind: preference; on_conflict/on_inapplicable/on_missing all unknown_no_penalty), not a development requirement or a hard exclusion. Its bound support is explicitly typed as provides_heuristic, and the interpretation states the inference as 'the_heuristic_is_the_line' with the line drawn at the upper edge of the class-typical range for the very class being screened. The critic's first finding attacks a position the rule does not take: nothing in the rule asserts that 500 g/mol is a developability ceiling, that larger molecules are undevelopable, or that permeability/absorption fails above it; the rule only ranks a candidate inside the class-typical band above one outside it. A soft ranking preference resting on a descriptive class-typical range is precisely the use a 'provides_heuristic' statement kind licenses, so the objection that the number is 'an inference' does not defeat it — the rule declares the inference openly rather than smuggling it in as a requirement. The second finding asserts counter-examples of clinically successful larger kinase inhibitors, but no cited claim supplies that counter-evidence, and in any case a ranking preference is not required to be a perfect discriminator; the rule's own falsification test frames that as an open empirical question rather than a defect in the rule's construction. Because the cutoff only orders candidates and never excludes them, and because the criterion's text states the lower edge is deliberately not applied, the proposal does not overreach the heuristic it cites.

meaning.definition: Fold by which the major circulating human metabolite inhibits VEGFR2 kinase activity less potently than the parent drug (metabolite potency divided by parent potency, expressed as fold-weaker). The quantity is read as a required-receptor coverage-attribution property: how far the circulating species that could contribute VEGFR2 engagement sits from the parent.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose major circulating metabolite is at least 10-fold weaker than the parent at VEGFR2 rank above candidates whose major metabolite is equipotent or stronger, because coverage of the required receptor remains parent-driven.
meaning.falsification_test: Collect metabolite potency data for the candidates; if candidates at or above the 10-fold ratio show the same measured VEGFR2 engagement at the tolerated dose as candidates below it, the cutoff does not discriminate and the criterion should be demoted to an unthresholded ordering.
meaning.rationale: VEGFR2 is one of the five required receptors, and this criterion asks which species carries that engagement: the cited report states that the major circulating metabolite accounts for approximately 17% of plasma radioactivity and inhibits VEGFR2 kinase activity approximately 10 times less potently than the parent, so in that case required-receptor coverage is carried by the dosed species and the metabolite contributes little. The 17% datum is read as making the ratio a margin rather than a coverage requirement: a candidate whose major circulating metabolite is at least that much weaker keeps VEGFR2 engagement attributable to the parent, while a metabolite that is equipotent or stronger, or that carries appreciable circulating exposure, introduces an unaccounted contributor to the required-receptor profile and is ranked lower. The passage reports a measured ratio, so the fold value is used directly and the bound is declared as an interpretation of that measurement, applied as a preference only, and the criterion is read alongside the VEGFR2 potency criterion rather than as that criterion.

meaning.definition: Reported steady-state clearance of the agent expressed as a percentage of liver blood flow, the scale on which clearance is conventionally classified as rapid versus moderate or low.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose reported clearance exceeds 70% of liver blood flow are demoted below agents with moderate-to-low clearance, enriching the shortlist for compounds whose oral exposure is not dominated by first-pass hepatic extraction.
meaning.falsification_test: Find an orally dosed agent against the required receptor set that is well tolerated and clinically effective despite a measured clearance above 70% of liver blood flow; that would show the class description's boundary does not separate developable from undevelopable candidates.
meaning.rationale: The objective requires an agent that engages the five receptors and has a pharmacological profile suitable for clinical development, and a hard constraint fixes the oral route; because oral dosing exposes the drug to hepatic first-pass extraction, clearance expressed on the liver-blood-flow scale is exactly the disposition quantity that decides how much of an oral dose reaches systemic circulation, so it measures the developability clause of the objective and is scored alongside, never instead of, the receptor criteria. Counter-evidence considered: the cited 70% boundary is offered as a classification rule of thumb rather than a requirement, high clearance is not by itself disqualifying for an oral agent (a substantial fraction of kinase inhibitors are rapidly eliminated and remain clinically used), and the survey from which the boundary comes tabulates rat elimination data alongside human values; the rule is therefore a preference ordering that demotes but never excludes, with unknown when no clearance value is reported. The heuristic is the line, and it ranks rather than qualifies.

meaning.definition: Number of independent elimination routes reported to contribute to the agent's disposition (an oxidative CYP route plus a second CYP isoform, an oxidative route supplemented by glucuronidation, or metabolic elimination supplemented by a non-hepatic route); a higher count indicates buffered clearance less sensitive to inhibition, induction or loss of any single pathway.
meaning.expected_change: Reorders candidates so that agents whose elimination rests on one documented route sink below agents with two or more independently documented routes; candidates with no route documentation receive unknown and are not penalised.
meaning.falsification_test: Retrieve the metabolic-route literature for the leading candidates and re-count routes from the retrieved texts; if every candidate ends with the same count (or none yields a count), the criterion carries no discriminating information for this candidate set.
meaning.rationale: Oral administration is a hard constraint, and an orally dosed agent whose clearance is buffered against metabolic perturbation is part of the pharmacological profile suitable for clinical development, so route redundancy serves the objective alongside target engagement and never substitutes for it. The five supporting claims are cited because they demonstrate that the property exists and varies within this exact space: members are described as metabolised mainly by CYP3A4 but also by CYP2C9, as oxidised via CYP3A4 with additional glucuronidation, as undergoing oxidative metabolism plus glucuronidation, and as metabolised in the liver with hepatobiliary excretion. The per-candidate integer is assembled from that same declared literature route run over the candidate names, so the criterion rests on the claims for the property and on the search for each count. Counter-evidence considered: even agents with several routes still show CYP-driven exposure shifts, so a higher count does not guarantee robustness and the rule is a preference only, never an exclusion, with unknown when the literature names no routes. No cited claim states a minimum number of independent routes for this class; the missing quantity is a class-specific threshold count of independently documented elimination routes.

The cited claim reports FGFR1 above 50% residual activity (weak/negligible) for the same compound, meaning the source compound itself would fail the required-receptor coverage; the proposal does not address this counter-evidence that the 25% line may exclude the very class it benchmarks.

The material counter-evidence finding is addressed head-on and it strengthens rather than undermines the bound: the cited panel reports that the same compound showed weak or negligible activity against FGFR1 (>50% residual activity) while the VEGFR/CSF1R-family kinases fell inside the <25% residual band, which is precisely the coverage failure this task screens for. The weakest-required-receptor design already captures that, and the proposal now states it, keeps the rule a preference with conflicts routed to human review, and retains the same source number and band.

claim_01M4YT0MTATBJMK4EEPVYZYSTF reports residual activity <25% for VEGFRs and CSF1R but >50% for FGFR1; the claim does not support a cutoff of <=25% for all five required receptors, as FGFR1 is explicitly outside that band.

The cited claim claim_01M4YT0MTATBJMK4EEPVYZYSTF reports potent inhibition (residual activity <25%) for VEGFRs and CSF1R, but the attribute requires the highest residual activity across all five required receptors; the claim does not provide data for FGFR1, and the source notes weak activity for FGFR1, so the cutoff of 25% is not supported for all required receptors.

Evidence-support finding resolved by taking the maximum only over the required receptors the panel actually reports: the 25% band is used exactly where the source applies it (VEGFRs and CSF1R), the omitted receptor stays unknown, and the source's own FGFR1 result is carried as the counter-example that motivates the preference rather than as an unsupported cutoff for a receptor the claim does not measure.

meaning.definition: Percent residual kinase activity of each required receptor (CSF1R, VEGFR1/FLT1, VEGFR2/KDR, VEGFR3/FLT4, FGFR1) measured in a single-concentration broad human receptor-kinase panel run at approximately 1 micromolar; the value ranked is the highest residual activity among the required receptors the panel actually reports, i.e. the weakest-engaged required receptor measured. A required receptor the panel does not report is unknown and does not enter the maximum. The authors' own bands are used: residual activity below 25% is called potent inhibition across VEGFRs (FLT1, FLT4, KDR) and type III RTKs including CSF1R, while above 50% residual activity is called weak or negligible.
meaning.expected_change: Down-ranks candidates whose single-concentration panel data show weak residual inhibition of a required receptor the panel reports, keeping candidates with potent engagement of every measured required receptor at 1 micromolar, without deleting anyone.
meaning.falsification_test: If a top-ranked candidate's own 1 micromolar panel reports above 50% residual activity for a required receptor and is still carried, the bound is not selecting for required-receptor engagement; likewise if the rule de-ranks agents whose required-receptor engagement is independently confirmed by potency data.
meaning.rationale: Single-concentration receptor-kinase panels are the first evidence produced for any multi-target kinase inhibitor and are the only source that reports several required receptors under one set of conditions. The cited passage bands the results itself: residual activity below 25% is called potent inhibition across VEGFRs (FLT1, FLT4, KDR) and type III RTKs including CSF1R, while above 50% residual activity (FGFR1, BTK, ROS, TIE2) is called weak or negligible. The band therefore covers the receptors the source measured; FGFR1 is the counter-example that shows why the criterion matters, since the profiled compound sits inside the potent band for the VEGFRs and CSF1R yet outside it for FGFR1, which is exactly the required-receptor coverage failure being screened for. Taking the maximum over the required receptors the panel reports isolates that failure mode without attributing an unmeasured value to a receptor the panel omitted. The rule stays a preference and conflicts route to human review, so a candidate failing one receptor on a single panel readout is de-ranked rather than deleted.

meaning.falsification_test: If retrieved sources for the leading candidates never report clearance against a creatinine-clearance boundary, the attribute returns unknown for all candidates; alternatively, if candidates documented as unchanged below the boundary still show dose-limiting accumulation in renal impairment, the direction of the ranking is wrong and the criterion should be reversed or withdrawn.
meaning.rationale: Oral administration is a hard constraint, and a chronically dosed oral agent whose clearance does not change with declining renal function is part of the profile suitable for clinical development, so renal independence is in scope; the attribute ranks candidates on it and does not replace the target-engagement criteria, and it is distinct from the registry's hepatic-impairment criterion. Counter-evidence considered: only one agent is documented as unaffected by renal impairment, and other kinase inhibitors may be renally cleared, so a documented boundary for one compound cannot be generalised as a class adequacy line; the attribute is therefore a preference ordering with unknown when no boundary is reported. The cutoff is the reported renal-function boundary down to which clearance is documented unchanged, read in the direction of ranking: a candidate shown unaltered to that boundary or lower is not more renal-dependent than the documented agent.

meaning.definition: The absolute magnitude of the change in oral exposure (AUC or absorbed fraction) produced by co-administration with food, pooled across reported fed-versus-fasted comparisons, irrespective of whether the change is an increase or a decrease; read as the absorption-robustness component of the pharmacological profile suitable for clinical development under the hard oral-route constraint.

meaning.falsification_test: Evidence that across this class meal-induced exposure changes of the reported magnitude are routinely managed by label wording without affecting efficacy or safety would refute treating the magnitude as a ranking axis.
meaning.rationale: The cited passages report fed-versus-fasted magnitudes in this class in both directions and by widely different amounts: one agent's exposure rises about 20% with food, another's combined parent-plus-metabolite exposure rises about 3.1-fold, another's AUC and Cmax rise up to about 10- and 17-fold, another's Cmax falls about 70%, two are reported as roughly doubling AUC with food, another reports AUC reductions of 22% and 32%, and others show no effect at all; the same literature also notes that meal-related changes are in practice managed by label wording and dosing instructions. Those numbers are magnitudes of fed-versus-fasted change, which is exactly the quantity this attribute pools, and each is taken from the report that states it rather than extrapolated. The criterion is a ranking axis over the observed magnitude and not a pass/fail bar; the quantity missing for a cutoff is a stated acceptable or unacceptable magnitude, so the rule orders and carries no cutoff. meaning.definition: Percentage reduction in maximum plasma concentration when the oral dose is taken with a high-fat meal compared with the fasted state, as reported in clinical studies (unit: %).
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose peak exposure drops least with a high-fat meal rank above meal-sensitive candidates, favouring agents whose oral absorption is not meal-dependent.
meaning.falsification_test: Show that the fed-versus-fasted peak-exposure change for a candidate does not translate into clinically meaningful exposure differences, or that no candidate in the pool has a documented meal effect.
meaning.rationale: Oral administration is a hard constraint, and an agent taken without regard to meals is part of the profile the objective asks for, so meal sensitivity of absorption is a developability property; the attribute ranks candidates on it and does not replace the target-engagement criteria. Counter-evidence considered: some orally dosed kinase inhibitors show no food effect at all, and a reduction of the size reported here has been managed clinically by dosing instructions rather than by withdrawal, so the line ranks and never excludes; whether a candidate's fed-state change translates into clinically meaningful exposure differences is exactly why the rule is a preference. This attribute reads Cmax, distinct from the registry's AUC-based meal criteria.

meaning.definition: Count of the five required tumour-microenvironment receptors (CSF1R, VEGFR1, VEGFR2, VEGFR3, FGFR1) for which a curated ChEMBL mechanism-of-action record asserts that the agent engages that target. The count runs over exactly the required set, so its ceiling is the receptor set the objective names and a missing record lowers the count without deleting the candidate. A mechanism record is an expert assertion carrying references, not a potency value; absence is unknown, never disengaged, because curation is sparse outside approved and late-stage drugs. The count is documentation breadth for the required set and is read alongside the registry's per-target curated potency criteria, which carry the quantitative engagement evidence.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with records spanning more of the five required receptors rank above those spanning fewer; candidates lacking records are neither excluded nor penalised, and partial-curation conflicts route to human review.
meaning.falsification_test: A candidate lacking records for a required receptor yet demonstrably engaging it at clinically relevant concentrations would show the count tracks curation density rather than engagement breadth; likewise if the count tracks approval status or study volume rather than engagement.
meaning.rationale: The count is taken over exactly the five receptors the objective requires, so its maximum is the objective's own coverage requirement and a lower count places a candidate lower on that dimension rather than scoring an unrelated property. The cited reports are cited for one class premise only: oral kinase inhibitors of this class document engagement of overlapping but different subsets of this receptor set (VEGFR1/2/3 with FGFR1/3 and c-FMS; VEGFR1/2 with CSF1R; VEGFR1/2/3 with FGFR1/2/3 but no CSF1R-family receptor), so the number of required receptors carrying a documented record varies within the class. The values themselves come from curated mechanism records, a curation independent of the activity table that reaches compound-target pairs with no pChEMBL value, whose absence yields unknown. Because a record asserts engagement and not strength, the count never substitutes for the registry's per-target potency criteria and never deletes a candidate; disagreements route to human review. No cited claim states a numeric coverage threshold (the missing quantity is how many of the five required receptors must carry a record), so the rule orders and carries no cutoff.

meaning.definition: Count of the five required receptors (CSF1R, VEGFR1, VEGFR2, VEGFR3, FGFR1) that a primary pharmacological report names in the tier it presents as the agent's primary or strongly inhibited targets, rather than in a secondary or additional tier. The tier is taken from the report's own wording; a required receptor the report places in a secondary tier, or does not tier, earns no credit and is not counted against the candidate.
meaning.expected_change: Candidates whose required receptors appear in the primary tier of their documented profile move above candidates whose required receptors appear only in a secondary tier, even when both name the same number of required receptors somewhere in the profile.
meaning.falsification_test: Re-extract the primary reports for a sample of candidates and re-code the tier of each required receptor; if the coded tiers do not track measured required-receptor potency, or independent coders cannot agree on the tier, the attribute carries no signal.
meaning.rationale: Primary reports tier an agent's kinase profile in their own words rather than listing it flatly, and the cited reports show the tier is reported consistently enough to code: VEGFR2, MET, AXL, RET, FLT3, KIT and TIE2 are listed as strongly inhibited with a separate secondary tier that includes VEGFR1, VEGFR3 and a CSF1R-family receptor; another agent is described as targeting RET, EGFR and VEGFR1/2/3 - particularly VEGFR2 - with FGFR1-4; others carry a long undifferentiated list in which the required receptors sit beside many non-required kinases. A required receptor named only in the secondary tier is weaker coverage evidence than one named in the primary tier, so the count is a measurable, ordinal property of the agent's own documented pharmacology, read over exactly the required set. No cited claim states a numeric primary-tier count or threshold, so the missing quantity is a stated primary-tier count and the rule ranks candidates without a cutoff.

schema: literature evidence yields numbers with units; a literature-bound attribute must be quantitative with a unit

The schema finding is resolved by making the attribute quantitative with a unit: the property is now the count of the five required receptors for which a report documents inhibition at a concentration it presents as clinically achievable, which is the same property read as a number rather than as a verdict. The bound is not invented: no cited claim states how many required receptors must be covered at clinically achievable concentrations, so the missing quantity is named and the rule ranks instead of thresholding.

claim_01M4YSGJ10X9MPVP4AENF8W0ZZ reports regorafenib inhibiting 18 kinases at clinically achievable concentrations, but the attribute counts only the five required receptors; the claim does not support the count for the required set.

The cited claims (e.g., claim_01M4YSGJ10X9MPVP4AENF8W0ZZ) report inhibitory effects at clinically achievable concentrations for regorafenib, but the attribute requires documentation for each of the five required receptors; the claim lists 18 kinases including VEGFR1-3 and FGFR1-2 but does not explicitly state that all five required receptors are covered at clinically achievable concentrations.

Evidence-support finding resolved by defining the count as a per-receptor credit count: a claim crediting VEGFR1-3 and FGFR1-2 at clinically achievable concentrations supplies credits for those receptors, a claim that the concentration needed for FGFR1 was quite high withholds the FGFR1 credit, and unaddressed receptors stay unknown - so the criterion no longer requires any single claim to cover all five required receptors at once.

meaning.definition: Number of the five required receptors (CSF1R, VEGFR1, VEGFR2, VEGFR3, FGFR1) for which a peer-reviewed report documents inhibitory activity of the agent or its active metabolites at a concentration the report itself presents as clinically achievable, as opposed to the receptor appearing only in a nominal target list. One receptor is credited only when a report states the activity at clinically achievable concentrations; a report stating that the concentration needed for a receptor is high counts against that receptor; a receptor with no such statement is unknown, not disengaged.
meaning.expected_change: Ranks candidates whose required receptors are documented as inhibited at clinically achievable concentrations above candidates whose receptors appear only in nominal target lists, without excluding anyone on an unquantified judgement.
meaning.falsification_test: Retrieve on-target pharmacodynamic data for candidates whose required receptors are only listed; if listed-only candidates achieve the same required-receptor inhibition at tolerated exposure as candidates with explicit clinically-achievable-concentration documentation, the count carries no information.
meaning.rationale: The criterion is a per-receptor credit count over exactly the five required receptors, so its ceiling is the objective's required set. The cited sources show the distinction it measures is reported and is not the same as a target list: an analysis counts the kinases actually inhibited at clinically achievable concentrations by an approved agent and its active metabolites (VEGFR1-3, KIT, PDGFR, FGFR1-2 and others) and separates them from the full 46-kinase panel, while a companion statement in the same source reports that for several kinases including FGFR1 the concentrations needed for effective inhibition were quite high. Each cited claim therefore contributes one or two credits to the count, and the count is a coverage summary over the required set rather than a claim that the source covered all five at once. No cited claim states how many of the five must be covered this way, so the missing quantity is a per-receptor coverage threshold and the rule orders candidates instead of cutting them off; a receptor the sources do not address is unknown, not discredited.

meaning.definition: Count (0-5) of the required receptors (CSF1R, VEGFR1, VEGFR2, VEGFR3, FGFR1) that one peer-reviewed report states are engaged or inhibited by the same agent, counted within that same publication; candidates documented as sparing a required receptor score below those documented as covering it.

matching_facets.statement: the four facets of the recovery rubric (handoff §12.2), read from executing fields; `gaps` lists what the records do not say

meaning.definition: Fraction of the administered oral dose recovered in urine, i.e. the renal contribution to total elimination and hence how far systemic exposure and clearance depend on renal function (unit: % of administered dose).
meaning.expected_change: Candidates with urinary recovery above the reported level are demoted relative to agents eliminated predominantly by non-renal routes, so the shortlist shifts toward compounds whose exposure is insensitive to renal function.
meaning.falsification_test: Show a candidate with high urinary recovery whose clearance is documented as unaffected by renal impairment, or one with very low urinary recovery whose clearance falls in renal impairment; either breaks the link between urinary recovery and the renal dependence the criterion screens for.
meaning.rationale: The objective requires an orally administered agent whose pharmacological profile is suitable for clinical development; because the agents will be given repeatedly by mouth to patients whose renal function varies, the share of the dose cleared renally fixes how far exposure and dosing depend on kidney function and is a developability property of the objective's second clause, scored alongside and never instead of receptor engagement. Counter-evidence considered: urinary recovery is a route-share observation for one agent and is not by itself proof that clearance is independent of renal function (renal secretion can matter even at low recovery, and the companion claim of unchanged clearance comes from a different compound), so the number ranks rather than qualifies and the rule is a preference, never an exclusion, with unknown when no recovery study is reported. The line is the reported route share of an orally dosed agent of this class, read in the direction of lower renal dependence.

meaning.definition: The least favourable reported half-maximal inhibitory concentration (nM) among the candidate's required receptors - CSF1R, VEGFR1 (FLT1), VEGFR2, VEGFR3 (FLT4) and FGFR1 - taken from whichever readout reports that receptor, whether a biochemical kinase assay or an intact-cell measure of the same receptor such as ligand-stimulated autophosphorylation or receptor-dependent proliferation. Values reported in nmol/L are read on the nM scale; the family is scored by its weakest member so that potency on one receptor cannot stand in for coverage of the set.
meaning.expected_change: Reorders candidates by the potency of their weakest required receptor, so a candidate that is sub-nanomolar on four required receptors but tens of nanomolar on the fifth falls behind a candidate whose worst required receptor is covered, and the five-member target set is scored as one coverage decision instead of five separate ones.
meaning.falsification_test: If candidates whose weakest required-receptor value is the least potent still show concurrent engagement of all five receptors in cells or in vivo at tolerated exposures, the weakest-member reduction overstates the requirement; and if biochemical and cellular member values rank the same candidates in opposite orders, the family is not one dimension and should be split back by target and assay format.
meaning.rationale: The required set is five receptors, and the objective asks for one agent that engages all five concurrently, so the decision quantity is the weakest member of the set rather than the average or the best: the attribute takes the highest (least potent) reported required-receptor IC50, which is exactly why aggregation is max. The cited literature supplies per-receptor nanomolar values for multi-target agents, including an agent covering all five required receptors, so the quantity is reported in the units and format the candidates will be read in.
